name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,567

clue.text: Your basic make-up is foundation

blocks.note: your genes are the basic material that makes you who you are
taken as written

explanation.surface: A beauty tip: foundation is the base layer of anyone's make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' and 'foundation' both look like cosmetics; here make-up is your inherited constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or beginning, the base from which something grows, much as a foundation underlies a building.

clue.text: Maybe helium's left inside balloon?

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other, here the letter for left within the word for helium's

blocks.note: helium is an example of a gas, plus the 's
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A party-trick question: is the helium escaping from inside the balloon?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a party balloon, but balloon here is a type of drinking vessel; GAS'S takes L after its first letter to give GLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A balloon is a large round-bowled brandy glass, so it is one example of a drinking vessel, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I wish it wasn't a mountain expedition - only at first, mind you

indicators.note: only at first means keep just the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.clueFragment: I wish it wasn't a mountain
blocks.note: the wish would be 'not a ben', a ben being a Scottish mountain
the opening letter of expedition

explanation.surface: A weary climber wishes the expedition were not up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: A ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: Nota bene is Latin for 'note well', used to draw attention to a point just like the phrase mind you.

clue.text: Impertinent fool stretches the bounds of stupidity

indicators.note: the outer letters stretch around the fool, holding it in between them
the bounds of a word are its two outermost letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of stupidity
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A cheeky idiot pushes his stupidity to its very limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy is informal for cheeky or disrespectful, a close synonym for being rude in one's manner.

clue.text: Half of hearing aids finally interpreting sign language

indicators.note: finally keeps only the last letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: semi- is the prefix meaning half
otic is the adjective for things relating to the ear
the last letter of aids

explanation.surface: Someone half-deaf uses hearing aids while finally learning to read sign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing aids' looks like one item, but it splits: 'of hearing' gives the ear adjective and 'aids' gives its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Semiotics is the study of signs and symbols and how meaning is read from them, so it covers interpreting any language of signs.

clue.text: Injured? Not hard with a sword, maybe

indicators.note: not hard says the letter standing for hard must be left out

blocks.note: to be harmed is to be injured
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Was anyone hurt? No, not badly, though somebody had a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: Being armed means carrying a weapon, and a sword is one example of such a weapon, hence the maybe.

clue.text: English priest in Rome wanting a Scottish doctor he's familiar with?

blocks.note: taken as written
a doctor you know well enough to call by first name, Dr Ian, Ian being the Scottish form of John

explanation.surface: An English priest in Rome is homesick for the Scottish family doctor he knows well.
explanation.walkthrough: Adrian IV, born Nicholas Breakspear, is the only English pope, the supreme priest in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope Adrian IV was the only Englishman ever to hold the papacy, the chief bishop of the Roman church.

clue.text: I felt satisfied while being hugged

indicators.note: something being hugged is held inside the arms of something else

blocks.note: a demand that is met has been satisfied
while can mean though, as in 'while I agree, ...'

explanation.surface: Someone recalls feeling content as they were embraced.
explanation.walkthrough: Methought is archaic, the past of methinks; 'I felt' must be read as a single verb phrase meaning it seemed to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Methought is the archaic past tense of methinks, meaning it seemed to me, so it serves as an old way to say I thought or felt.

clue.text: Father's middle daughter falls for new beau

indicators.note: falls for here means gives way to, so one letter drops out and another takes its place
middle pins down which of the repeated letters is swapped: the central one

blocks.note: daddy is a word for father
D is the abbreviation for daughter
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A father's middle daughter falls in love with a new boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle' picks which D goes: the central one of DADDY is replaced by N.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau in its older sense is a fashionable man much concerned with clothes, exactly what a dandy is.

clue.text: Flares set off by officer in the open

indicators.note: flares that are set off explode and scatter, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
CO stands for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An officer launches signal flares out in open country.
explanation.definitionFit: Al fresco is borrowed from Italian and describes doing something outdoors, such as eating under the sky.

clue.text: Was hurdling a field sport?

blocks.note: a lea is a field or meadow, a poetic word
PT is physical training, school sport

explanation.surface: A question whether hurdles counts as a field sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurdling is a track event, which is why the question mark is there; the clue splits after 'hurdling'.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap is to jump over something, so someone who leapt was clearing an obstacle just as a hurdler does.

clue.text: A mantra is stirring for a listener

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters before it are mixed into another order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A meditator finds a mantra moving to someone who hears it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Samaritans is a UK charity whose volunteers answer phone calls from people in distress and listen.
explanation.definitionFit: A Samaritan volunteer's whole job is lending a sympathetic ear to callers, so the person is a listener by role.

clue.text: Bush grew bark

blocks.note: rose is a past tense meaning increased or grew
a hound bays, a deep howling bark

explanation.surface: A shrub got bigger and covered itself in bark.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush and bark both pull towards trees; bark is the dog's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay is the name of shrubs such as the rhododendron and oleander, so it names a kind of flowering bush.

clue.text: Colourful words including one between yellow and blue

indicators.note: between puts one piece in the gap separating two others

blocks.note: or is the heraldic name for gold or yellow
a means one, as in a single thing
blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative or Tory party

explanation.surface: A painter's vivid language includes a shade lying between yellow and blue on the spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The colours look like a spectrum (green lies between yellow and blue), but they are heraldic yellow and the Tory blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratory is the art of eloquent public speaking, whose rich and vivid speech can fairly be called colourful language.

clue.text: Maybe armour's best feature

blocks.note: first meaning: a suit that is strong, of which plate armour is an example
second meaning: the quality someone excels at

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is': armour is an example of the first sense, and is also the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a sturdy suit of protective clothing, and idiomatically, from card games, the area where a person excels most.

clue.text: Protect one who wrongly accepts tokens of commitment?

blocks.note: a wedding or engagement ring is a pledge of commitment
a fence is a dealer who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Guarding against someone who dishonestly takes engagement rings.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as a whole cryptic picture: a fence handling stolen rings would be a ring fence.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring-fence money or resources is to guarantee they are kept for one purpose and shielded from other use.

clue.text: High sturdy walls the usual support for a window cleaner?

indicators.note: walls here is a verb: the first piece surrounds the second as walls enclose a space

blocks.note: stout means sturdy and strong

blocks.clueFragment: the usual support for a window cleaner
blocks.note: a window cleaner stands on a ladder rung

explanation.surface: Tall solid walls are what a window cleaner normally leans his ladder against.
explanation.walkthrough: High looks like the height of a building, but it means intoxicated; STOUT splits as ST-RUNG-OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Strung out is slang for being under the influence of drugs, which is what high means in the drug sense.

clue.text: Breakfast for one - guests cleared out

indicators.note: cleared out means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer shell of the word

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, for one
guests with its insides removed

explanation.surface: A B&B host serves breakfast to one diner after the other guests have left.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs are a classic morning meal, so they serve as an example of breakfast, the sort of dish served first thing.

clue.text: Poet's not doing so well raising small children

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something puts it higher, so those letters go at the top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
CH is the abbreviation for children
iller means sicker, not as well

explanation.surface: A poet is struggling while bringing up young children.
explanation.walkthrough: Friedrich Schiller was the German poet who wrote the Ode to Joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Schiller was an eighteenth-century German writer of verse and drama, best known for the Ode to Joy, so he is a poet.

clue.text: Cook puts on fancy manners away from the servants' quarters

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, so the word after it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as fodder
putting on airs means adopting affected, fancy manners

explanation.surface: The cook adopts posh manners when away from the kitchen and servants' rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook looks like the household servant; it is the anagram signal. In big houses, servants lived downstairs and the family above.
explanation.definitionFit: In a grand house the staff worked below stairs, so the family's floors upstairs were the part away from where servants lived.

clue.text: Beastly noise the reason tattooist might stop?

blocks.note: a tattooist would have to stop with nothing, O, of ink left

explanation.surface: Does an animal's grunt make the tattoo artist pause?
explanation.walkthrough: O stands for zero, so O INK is no ink, the reason a tattooist has to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting sound a pig makes, and a pig is a beast, so the word is an animal's noise.

clue.text: He'll find fault to repair on bridge

indicators.note: in an across entry, putting one thing on another means it comes after it

blocks.note: to bridge a river is to cross it
to patch something is to mend it

explanation.surface: An engineer inspecting a bridge will find faults to fix.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is a bad-tempered, grumpy person, the kind who complains and criticises constantly.

clue.text: Pick up faint broadcast in the ether

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: faint light is dim
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A radio ham picks up a weak signal transmitted over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' and 'broadcast' suggest radio reception; only broadcast plays that role.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether is a poetic word for the upper sky, so something in the ether is suspended up above the ground.

clue.text: Simple coat's reversible hood

indicators.note: a reversible coat can be turned inside out, here the letters are turned end to end

blocks.note: naif means naive or simple
an animal's coat is its fur

explanation.surface: A plain coat has a hood that can be worn either way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Hood looks like part of the coat; it is short for hoodlum.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood is slang short for hoodlum, a violent thug or gangster, which is also what a ruffian is.

clue.text: Something puzzling about public transport

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: There is something baffling about the way public transport runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a word puzzle where pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables, so it is a kind of brain teaser.

clue.text: Keep coming over chilled at Iceland stores

indicators.note: something that stores goods holds them within it, so the letters are inside these words
coming over suggests turning over, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the letters running across the join of these words

explanation.surface: Frozen goods kept chilled at the Iceland supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: Iceland is a British frozen-food supermarket chain. Keep is a noun: the strongest tower of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, a stronghold, which is what a citadel is.

clue.text: Catholic to have another look at his belief

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic
to redo something is to go over it again

explanation.surface: A Catholic reconsiders his faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith, from the Latin word meaning I believe that opens the Creed.

clue.text: Legendary bowler - one might fall for a duck

definitions.text: one might fall for a duck

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Francis ..., who by legend finished his game of bowls before fighting the Armada

blocks.clueFragment: one might fall for a duck
blocks.note: second meaning: a male duck, which would fall in love with a female one

explanation.walkthrough: Bowler and duck both suggest cricket, where a duck is a batsman out for no runs; neither sense is meant. Bowls is a lawn game of rolling balls at a target.
explanation.definitionFit: The Elizabethan sea captain is famed for his game of bowls on Plymouth Hoe, and the same word names a male duck.

clue.text: Indian IT hub running on algebra

indicators.note: running suggests a mix of letters in motion, put into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: An Indian technology centre runs on mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern city of Bengaluru, formerly so named, is famous as the centre of India's software and technology industry.

clue.text: That is providing cover for Vogue?

definitions.text: That is providing cover for Vogue?

indicators.note: providing cover for something means wrapping round it, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
Vogue is an example of a magazine, mag for short

explanation.surface: Something is supplying the front page of a fashion magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a cover photo is what wraps a magazine like Vogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine's cover is a striking photograph, so a picture of this kind is exactly what provides it.

clue.text: Ray's bottom is starting to get dirty

indicators.note: the bottom, the final letter of the name, now starts the word instead of ending it

blocks.note: Ray Mears is a British TV survival and bushcraft expert

explanation.surface: A fish's underside is beginning to get grubby.
explanation.walkthrough: Ray looks like the fish; it is the first name of Ray Mears, a British wilderness-skills presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To smear something is to dirty it with a greasy or sticky streak, so the verb is a synonym of soil.

clue.text: Foot is to toe as inch is to chin?

indicators.note: inch and chin hold the same letters in another order, so the words before must likewise be rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: It reads like an analogy question from an exam about body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The analogy shape hides the split: Foot is the definition, and the second half tells you to scramble the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tootsie is a playful, childish word for a foot or toe, so it can stand for a foot in nursery speech.
